# User guide: Home and agent storage

## In plain words

The plugin keeps two kinds of data on your server. The first is the home: the sign-ins, memory and chat history of each agent. The second is agent storage: the program files of the agents you install. The plugin does not write this data to disk file by file. It keeps it in a few compressed files called layers, and it catches your day-to-day changes in a writable layer on top. This design protects your USB flash drive from constant small writes. On a boot disk that is not a USB flash drive, a home does not need layers: it can be **plain folders**, an ordinary folder with no saves and no tidy-ups. On an internal boot disk, a new agent also installs as plain folders unless **Agent storage** is set to **Compressed layers**. You choose where the layers live, how the writable layer works, and when the plugin saves. This page explains each choice and what to do when the plugin asks for your attention.

## The basics

### Home and agent storage

| Piece | What it holds | Can the plugin rebuild it? |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Home** | For each Unraid user: agent sign-ins, settings, memory, chat transcripts, Config Hub state and secrets. | No. Keep a backup. See [Home backup and restore](backup-restore.md). |
| **Agent storage** | The installed program files of every agent. | Yes. The plugin installs the agent again by itself when the files are missing. |

Each user has one home. Each agent has one set of files in agent storage. Agent storage always uses a single layer.

### Layers and the writable layer

A **layer** is one compressed, read-only file (a SquashFS image: a file that holds a whole folder tree in compressed form). The plugin joins the layers and shows them to the agent as one normal folder.

On top of the layers sits one **writable layer**. Every change an agent makes goes there first. A change can be a new chat line, a settings edit or a downloaded file.

Two actions move the data down into layers:

- **Save** (the card button is called **Save now**). The plugin writes the changes in the writable layer into one small, new layer. Nothing closes. The plugin frees the writable layer at once, or when the last workspace of the home closes.
- **Merge** (the card button is called **Merge layers**). The plugin joins all layers and the unsaved changes into one single layer. It closes the open workspaces of that home for a short time to do this.

Each save adds a layer. Many layers slow the first load and use more memory. A merge brings the count back to one.

### Why layers

A USB flash drive wears out when programs write many small files to it. An agent writes all day. If it wrote straight to the drive, the drive would fail early.

With layers, the agent writes to the writable layer. The plugin writes to the drive only when it saves. One save writes one file in one go. This keeps the wear low. It also protects against power loss in the middle of a save: the plugin writes a layer completely before it uses it, and old layers stay until the new layer is safe.

## Where to find it

Open the **AI CLI Agents** page under Unraid's Settings menu. It has these tabs: **Configuration**, **Agent Store**, **Storage**, **Config Hub**, **Agent Relay** and **Debug Console**.

| What you want | Where it is |
| :-- | :-- |
| Choose where home and agent data live | **Configuration** tab, card **Storage**, fields **Where homes are stored** and **Where agents are stored** (button **Change…**) |
| Choose the writable layer for homes | **Configuration** tab, field **Where unsaved changes are kept** |
| Choose how homes are stored | **Configuration** tab, field **Home storage** |
| Choose how agents are stored | **Configuration** tab, field **Agent storage** |
| Choose how often the plugin saves | **Configuration** tab, field **Save unsaved home changes every** |
| Choose when the plugin merges | **Configuration** tab, field **Merge layers after** |
| See where the boot disk space goes, and free it | **Storage** tab, card **Boot disk space**. It includes homes and agents from their configured storage paths. See "Boot disk space" below. |
| See, save, merge, repair or delete a home | **Storage** tab, section **Homes**: one card for each home |
| See the size of an agent's files | The agent's card in the **Agent Store** tab. See [Agent Store](agent-store.md). |
| See storage warnings | The Health dot near the top of the Settings page. See [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md). |
| Get help when storage is missing | The terminal page. The drawer shows **Emergency Session**. |

The **Storage** tab has three kinds of card: one card for each home, the card **Boot disk space**, and the card **System memory**. Each card has the same header: a button to open and close the card, a one-line status, an **(i)** button with help, and a menu to move the card. The cards start in this order: the homes, **Boot disk space**, **System memory**. The tab remembers the order and which cards you closed, in this browser only. The menu item **Reset layout** puts the cards back.

The card **System memory** shows how much of Unraid's own memory (the RAM disk, where Unraid keeps its system files) is used. Its status reads, for example, "41 % of 7.8 GB used". The card is closed while the use is under 80 %, and it opens by itself above that. A full bar is a problem for the whole server, not only for this plugin. Save the unsaved home changes, or move the agent temporary files to a pool.

## Choosing where to keep storage

### The advice, in order

Pick a place for **Where homes are stored** and **Where agents are stored** in this order:

1. **A cache pool path**, for example `/mnt/cache/appdata/aicliagents`. This is the fastest and safest choice. The picker marks it **recommended** when it is open to you.
2. **An Unassigned Devices path**, for example `/mnt/disks/mydrive/aicliagents`. Use this when you have a spare drive that is not in the array or a pool. Use a folder inside the device. The plugin refuses the top folder of the device itself, so the storage picker lists each drive as its `aicliagents` folder.
3. **A single array disk**, for example `/mnt/disk1`. This works, but the disk spins up on every save. The picker lists array disks as **advanced**.
4. **`/mnt/user`**, a user share. Use it only when none of the other places is open to you. For example, you have no cache pool and no spare drive, and your share spans more than one disk.
5. **The USB flash drive.** This is the fallback and the default on a fresh install. It works everywhere, but it wears. The picker lists it near the end.

A home must not live on a network share (under `/mnt/remotes`). The picker shows such a share as **unavailable** for home storage. Do not use one for agent storage either.

### Why `/mnt/user` comes last

Paths 1 to 3 write straight to a disk. A path under `/mnt/user` goes through Unraid's shared-folder layer. Its short name is shfs. Shfs has only about 10 worker threads. Heavy save or merge activity through it can slow down or freeze the whole server, not only this plugin.

The plugin does not block `/mnt/user`, because some servers have no other choice. It shows a yellow advice box instead. If your share is set to use one pool only (the share setting **Use cache pool** is **Only**), the plugin stores the direct pool path. Your data then never passes through shfs. The picker shows a note such as "stored on the pool, not /mnt/user".

### Move storage to another place

> [!WARNING]
> A move copies your data to the new place and then switches to it. The plugin saves and merges first, and it checks every file after the copy. It does not delete the old data until the copy is safe. A large home can take several minutes. Open workspaces on that home close during the move.

Wait for a **Home storage** or **Agent storage** conversion to finish before you move storage. The plugin refuses a move while the conversion is queued or running.

1. Open the **Configuration** tab.
2. Press **Change…** next to **Where homes are stored** or **Where agents are stored**. Expect: a panel opens and the plugin probes your storage targets.
3. Read the list. Each line shows a name, a path and small chips: the type of place, the free space, and warnings.
4. Choose one line. Or choose **Custom path…** and type a path, for example one that starts with `/mnt/`. The **Browse** button next to the field opens a folder browser. The plugin checks a custom path when you leave the field. Expect: "Valid target", or a reason for the refusal.
5. Press **Move storage here**. Expect: a confirmation titled **Migrate Storage?**. It shows the old and new paths and the list of files with their sizes.
6. Press **Yes, Migrate**. Expect: your open workspaces close, and a message **Storage move started**. Press **OK**. The page reloads. The plugin copies the files in the background, so you can close the page. Watch the row **Moving storage to …** in the activity tray. The path setting changes when the copy is done.

Press **Cancel** in the confirmation to keep the old place. The path field goes back to the old value. On a phone, the picker and the halt cards (below) fit the screen, and the halt buttons fill a full row.

| Chip or badge in the picker | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- |
| **recommended** | The best open choice. Only one line has it. |
| **current** | Your data is here now. |
| **advanced** | A single array disk. It works but spins up the disk. |
| **unavailable** | The plugin refuses this place, for example a network share for a home. You cannot select it. |
| **HDD — spins on every persist** | An array disk or hard disk. Each save wakes it. |
| **RAM-backed — data lost on reboot** | The place is in memory. The plugin refuses it. |
| **no symlinks/xattrs** | The file system lacks features the plugin needs. |
| **on /mnt/user — see advice below** | The shfs advice applies. |

If a pool or the array holds your storage, the field shows a note under it. A note "On array — unavailable when stopped. Emergency mode will activate." appears for the array. A note "On pool 'name' — unavailable if pool is stopped." appears for a pool.

### Move a home off a USB flash drive

When a home's data sits on a real USB flash drive and a durable disk exists, the home card shows a green strip: "This data is on a USB flash drive — move it to a durable disk (faster, no USB wear)" with the button **Move off USB flash drive**.

1. Press **Move off USB flash drive**. Expect: a list of durable disks with their free space.
2. Choose a disk. The dialog shows an estimate of the time (about two minutes for each gigabyte, at least two minutes).
3. Close the terminals of that user first. If you do not, the copy waits until the home is idle.
4. Press **Move data**. Expect: "Move started". The plugin copies the layers, checks them, and then switches the path. The USB drive is untouched until the check passes.

An internal boot drive in a server that boots from a ZFS pool is not a USB flash drive. The strip does not show there.

### Convert a home to plain folders

Layers are for a USB flash drive. When the boot disk is not a USB flash drive, the plugin already keeps anything new as plain folders. A home that had layers before stays layered, and it keeps needing saves and tidy-ups. A tidy-up needs room for a new layer beside the old ones, so on a small boot disk it can fail again and again. The conversion ends this.

When a home has layers and its folder is not on a USB flash drive, the home card shows a green strip: "This home can change to plain folders. Then it needs no more saves or tidy-ups." with the button **Convert to plain folders**.

1. Press **Convert to plain folders**. Expect: a dialog **Convert to plain folders?** that says:
   - every workspace of this home closes and opens again;
   - the home stays on the boot disk;
   - it needs no more tidy-ups;
   - your current storage files are kept as a backup for 14 days, then removed. When the boot disk is short of space, that backup is kept on another disk.
2. Press **Convert**. Expect: "Conversion queued". Press **Cancel** to stop. Nothing changes then.
3. Watch the Activity tray. The pill names each step: "Closing workspaces", "Checking space", "Copying the home", "Freeing the boot disk", "Copying the home back", "Switching to plain folders", "Opening workspaces again". On a boot disk with enough room, the steps "Freeing the boot disk" and "Copying the home back" do not occur.
4. When it is done, the pill says "The home now uses plain folders. It needs no more tidy-ups." The workspaces open again by themselves.

The plugin copies the home with every workspace closed. It does not save or merge first, so it needs no extra room for a new layer. When the boot disk has no room for the copy, the plugin copies the home to a work folder on another disk first. It then moves the old layers to that work folder, which frees the boot disk, and copies the home back. If a step fails, the plugin puts the old layers back, and the home is exactly as before. The work folder is the setting **Work folder for storage jobs**. See "The field "Work folder for storage jobs"" below. A conversion that needs the work folder does not start while the array is stopped.

The plugin never overwrites files that are already in the plain folder of the home. If that folder holds files, the conversion stops and changes nothing. The Activity tray then says, for example: "Could not finish. Refused: the plain folder /mnt/cache/aicliagents/passthrough/homes/root already has files (first: notes.txt). Move them away, then try again. Nothing was changed." Move or archive the named files, then press **Convert to plain folders** again. Small empty marker files that the plugin keeps in the hidden folder `.aicli` do not count as files.

This conversion changes one home. It does not change the setting **Home storage**. After it, the line under **Home storage** on the **Configuration** tab reads, for example, **Mixed: 1 of 2 homes are plain folders**. To convert the other homes, press the button under that line, or choose **Plain folders** in **Home storage**.

The home stays on the boot disk, so the plugin works while the array is stopped. Backups work as before. A home on a USB flash drive is never offered the conversion; use **Move off USB flash drive** for that. Agents have their own conversion. See "Convert agents to plain folders" below.

You can also start the conversion from the notice in the Activity tray (see "The notice to close workspaces") or from the Unraid notification "AICliAgents: homes can move to plain folders". That notification comes once after a plugin install or update when one or more homes can convert. It comes again only when that set of homes changes. Its link opens this dialog for the first such home.

### Agents on an internal boot disk

The program files of an agent follow the same rule as a home. On a USB boot stick, every agent keeps compressed layers. On an internal boot disk (for example a small ZFS mirror), a new agent installs as **plain folders**. Plain folders start faster and need no merges. They also use more space on the boot disk, because a layer is compressed more than a folder is. Open **Configuration** and look at **Agent storage**. Choose **Compressed layers** when your boot disk is small. Then new installs and updates use layers again. Choosing it converts the agents that are in plain folders back to layers, as the dialog explains.

When the boot disk has no room for a new agent, the install stops and says "No space on the boot disk". The message names the **Boot disk space** card on the Storage tab and the setting **Agent storage**. The version in use stays.

### Convert agents to plain folders

An agent that was installed with layers stays layered until you convert it. The conversion is offered on an internal boot disk while **Agent storage** is not set to **Compressed layers**, and when at least one agent has layers. The setting **Agent storage** then shows **Mixed** until you convert the rest. It is not offered on a USB boot stick.

1. On the **Boot disk space** card (see "Boot disk space" above), press **Convert to plain folders** on the line **Agents: current versions**. Expect: a dialog **Convert agents to plain folders?**.
2. Read the dialog before you press anything. It lists each agent with **Size now** and **As plain folders**. Below the list it shows the extra space, the free space now and the free space after. The size as plain folders is an estimate: the size of the layer files times 5.8, divided by the compression of the boot disk. The dialog does not measure anything. It shows the numbers of the last measure, with the line "Measured at 14:05 (3 min ago)". When the numbers are more than 10 minutes old, or there are none, the dialog shows the button **Measure now**. Press it once, wait for the measure to end, and the dialog opens again with new numbers.
3. Tick or untick agents. The totals change at once.
4. Press **Convert**. Expect: "Conversion queued". Press **Cancel** to stop. Nothing changes then.

The dialog refuses when less than 10% of the boot disk, or less than 2 GB, would stay free after the conversion. It says how many MB are missing, and the button **Convert** stays off. Remove old versions or left-over files first, then open the dialog again.

The plugin converts one agent at a time. It closes only the workspaces that run this agent, copies the agent, checks the copy, and switches. The workspaces open again by themselves. The Activity tray names each step: "Closing the workspaces of this agent", "Measuring the agent", "Copying the agent to a plain folder", "Moving the old layers aside", "Switching the agent to plain folders", "Opening workspaces again". If a step fails, the plugin puts the old layers back and the agent is as before.

The old layers move to a backup folder. They stay for 14 days, then the plugin removes them. They use space until then. You can remove them sooner with **Remove** on the **Left over** line.

## The settings "Home storage" and "Agent storage"

**Home storage** and **Agent storage** are two settings on the **Configuration** tab. Each setting has two choices. **Compressed layers** stores changes in compressed layers and a writable layer. **Plain folders** stores files directly in ordinary folders. **Home storage** applies to the homes. **Agent storage** applies to the program files of the agents. New homes use **Home storage**. New agent installs and updates use **Agent storage**.

Under each setting, the line **Now:** shows what is true on disk, not only what the setting says. It reads **Plain folders**, **Compressed layers**, or **Mixed**. An example is **Mixed: 1 of 2 homes are plain folders**. The line changes when you convert one home with **Convert to plain folders** on its card. When a setting is mixed, a button appears: **Convert the other 1 home to plain folders**. Press it to finish the change for the items that are left.

### Change one setting

> [!WARNING]
> This change closes open workspaces and converts saved storage. It converts only the kind you changed: homes for **Home storage**, agents for **Agent storage**. Items that are already on the new choice stay as they are. The conversion can take several minutes. Keep the server running until the status says the migration is complete.

1. Open the **Configuration** tab.
2. Change **Home storage** or **Agent storage**. Expect: the dialog **Change home storage?** or **Change agent storage?** explains the conversion.
3. Read the space check. It uses a complete **Boot disk space** report from the last 10 minutes and current free space. It counts the new storage and the copies needed to restore the old storage for every item it will convert. It keeps at least 2 GB or 10% of each disk free, whichever is larger. It leaves out the other kind and the items that are already on the new choice. If the report is missing, old or incomplete, refresh it on the **Boot disk space** card. If there is not enough room, the message gives the required and available space. No workspace closes and no data changes. The status keeps the refusal message.
4. Press **Convert homes** or **Convert agents**. Expect: the confirmation closes when the conversion starts. A status appears under the settings. It names the kind, shows the target, the current item and the number of completed items.
5. Wait for **Home storage migration complete** or **Agent storage migration complete**. The saved setting changes only after all items of that kind convert. Workspaces that ran before the change open again after success or a complete put-back, even when **Auto-launch workspaces** is off.

When every item of the kind is on the new choice already, the plugin only saves the setting. No workspace closes.

If this page stays open while another tab changes a setting, the next save uses the completed value. It does not start the same conversion again.

If the server stops during conversion, Configuration and **Boot disk space** show the changed items. Press **Continue** to finish the change. Press **Put back** to restore the changed items to the saved choice. Workspaces and storage actions stay paused until recovery ends.

**Dismiss** hides only the result for that conversion. A later conversion appears and disables both settings while it runs.

You can open another page while the conversion runs. The **Boot disk space** card also shows the progress and says which kind converts. It disables actions that could change storage during the conversion. Automatic workspace launches wait until the conversion ends. Return to **Configuration** or **Storage** to see the same status. The page does not block navigation.

The migration of homes includes homes with saved layers, files in a plain home folder or a saved workspace. A user account without saved home storage does not add an item to the migration.

Copies kept when a setting changes from plain folders to compressed layers appear in **Boot disk space** under **Left over**. Each row shows its size and age. You can remove a copy after no conversion needs it. The plugin does not remove these copies automatically.

The plugin pauses automatic saves, merges and queued storage jobs during the conversion. A storage job that already holds a lock can finish. The migration waits and retries the affected item for a limited time.

The migration also waits for an agent installation that was already running. While the migration is queued, running or rolling back, the **Agent Store** refuses new installs, upgrades, restores from a kept backup and removals. It shows: “Wait for the storage migration to finish before installing, removing, or upgrading agents.” Try again after the migration ends.

If another storage job is using an agent or home, the plugin names that item and refuses before it closes workspaces. Wait for the job to finish, then try again. If a conversion fails after it starts, the status names the item and gives a short reason. The Debug Console keeps the lower-level detail. The plugin keeps the previous setting when it restores the converted items. Read the final message before you try again.

## The setting "Where unsaved changes are kept"

This setting decides where the writable layer of each home lives. It applies to homes only. Agents keep their own rule.

| Choice | What it means | Good for | Cost |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **RAM (zram): fast, no disk wear, lost on a crash until saved** | Changes live in compressed memory (zram: a block of RAM that stores data in compressed form). | Flash drives and fast work. This is the default. | A crash or power cut loses the changes since the last save. |
| **Disk: survives a crash or power cut, uses space on the persistence drive** | Changes are written to a folder on the same drive as the layers. | Servers that crash, or that have a durable pool. | It uses space and makes more writes to that drive. |

**Disk** is refused when your storage sits on a USB flash drive. The server answers **RAM** there, because disk writes would wear the drive. **RAM** is refused when a home is bigger than 80 percent of the RAM area. The warning names the sizes.

The setting applies when **Home storage** is **Compressed layers**. Homes in **Plain folders** have no writable layer. They write straight to the chosen path.

### Switch the setting

> [!WARNING]
> A change moves data. The plugin closes your open workspaces, saves each home into a checked layer, and mounts the home again. This can take several minutes for a large home. Do not reload the page and do not restart the server during the move. The plugin deletes nothing. The old writable layer holds only what the checked save already contains.

1. Open the **Configuration** tab.
2. Change **Where unsaved changes are kept**. Expect: a check runs, then a warning titled **Move the writable layer to RAM?** or **Move the writable layer to disk?**
3. Read the warning. It lists each home on its own line, for example "root: now on disk, will move (1880 MB)". A yellow box says "Your open workspaces will be closed while the data moves." when something must move.
4. Press **Close workspaces and move**. If nothing needs to move, the button reads **Save setting**. Expect: a screen "Moving writable layers to RAM..." (or "disk...") with a bar.
5. Wait for **Writable layer changed**. The page reloads.
6. Open your workspaces again. The plugin saved each workspace's place, so **Resume** brings the conversation back.

Any other way to close the warning cancels the change. **Cancel** and the Escape key put the setting back to its saved value. A click outside the warning does not close it. The setting shows the new value while the warning is open. It goes back when you cancel.

If a home cannot move, the plugin puts the setting back. It shows **Not moved** with the name of the home and the reason, for example that the home is in use or that there is no room. If the old writable layer still holds changes that the save did not capture, the reason says so. A chat file that the save stored in a layer no longer blocks the move. Your data stays where it was.

## The home storage card

The **Storage** tab shows one card for each user that has a home. The title of the card is **Home:** and the name of the user. Click the title to open or close the card. A card with many fields is easy to misread, so this table lists each one.

| Field | What it shows |
| :-- | :-- |
| Title (top left) | The Unraid user that owns the home. |
| Status line (in the header) | One line that stays visible when you close the card. A home in plain folders reads "Plain folders on the boot disk · no saves needed". A layered home reads, for example, "12 layers · 240 MB unsaved", or "12 layers · no unsaved changes". A home that is not mounted starts with "Not mounted". While a job runs, the line ends with the job, for example "Saving…". |
| **(i)** in the header | Says what a home is and what the buttons of the card do. A layered home and a home in plain folders get different texts. |
| "N MB persisted · N Layers" (top of the body) | The size of all saved layers and how many there are. For a home in plain folders: "Plain folders on" and the folder. |
| Status word (top of the body) | **Plain folders**: the home is an ordinary folder. It has no layers, no save button and no merge button. **Layered**: nothing is unsaved. **N MB volatile**: that much unsaved data is in RAM. **N MB writable**: that much unsaved data is in the writable layer on disk. **OFFLINE**: the home is not mounted. |
| Bar | A home in plain folders has no bar and no note in the body. Its status line in the header says "Plain folders on the boot disk · no saves needed". For a layered home with a RAM writable layer: how full the RAM area is, with the text "N% ZRAM used". For a disk writable layer: the text "N MB durable writable layer". The disk layer has no fixed size, so the bar never shows a false percentage. |
| Mount line | The folder where the plugin shows the home to the agents. |
| Folder line | The folder that holds the layer files. |
| Orange tile | The unsaved changes. In RAM mode it reads "ZRAM changes (volatile, not yet flushed)". In disk mode it reads "Writable changes (durable, not yet compacted)". |
| Layer rows | One row per layer with its file name and size. |
| Old layers row | Appears only after **Convert to plain folders**, while the plugin keeps the old layers for a rollback. It reads "Old layers kept for rollback: 5.00 MB, removed automatically on 5 Nov 2026" and has the button **Remove old layers**. The date is the day the plugin removes the layers by itself. See "Remove the old layers" below. |
| Backup row | The state of the backup of this home and the button **Backup…**. The row reads, for example, "Backup: not yet · to /mnt/datapool/backups", "Backup: last 12 Oct 2026, 02:00 · 3.1 MB (warm)", or "Backup: not set up.". The **(i)** beside the button says what a backup is: a second, plain copy of the home in a folder you choose. Damage to the boot disk does not reach it. It is a copy of the home folder (the settings, sign-ins and history of the agents), not a backup of the server. See [Home backup and restore](backup-restore.md). |

A badge **Awaiting idle** (with an hourglass) means the plugin wants to merge this home but waits until no terminal uses it. A home in plain folders never shows this badge.

### The four buttons

The buttons have words. They sit at the bottom of the card, and each is 44 px high on a phone. Hold a finger on a button, or hover with a mouse, to read its tooltip.

| Button | What it does | Closes workspaces? |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Save now** | Saves the writable layer into one new layer. | No |
| **Merge layers** | Saves the unsaved changes and merges all layers into one. | Yes, for a short time. Each workspace reopens by itself. |
| **Repair** | Unmounts and mounts the home's storage again. It shows only when the home is not mounted. | It can interrupt open workspaces. |
| **Delete home…** (red) | Deletes the whole home. A dialog asks you to confirm first. | Not allowed while a workspace or a storage job uses the home. |

All buttons are off while a job runs on that home. The lock comes from the server, so it holds on every device and browser tab. **Merge layers** is also off, with the tooltip "Nothing to merge: one layer and no unsaved changes", when there is nothing to merge. A home in plain folders shows only **Repair** (when it is not mounted) and **Delete home…**.

#### Save now

1. Press **Save now**. Expect: a dialog **Persist Home Changes?**.
2. Press **Persist Now**. Expect: "Queued — watch the activity tray for progress."
3. Watch the Activity tray at the bottom right. A pill shows the job: queued, running, done.

A save does not close anything. If workspaces are still open, the memory number may stay high after the save. The data is safe on disk. The tray then says "Saved to flash — ~N MB stays in RAM until this home's open sessions close." The plugin frees that memory when the last workspace of the home closes.

If the home has no changes since the last save, the message is **Nothing to save**. This is a neutral message, not a success and not an error. The Activity tray says the same for a save that waited in the queue.

A second save inside 30 minutes of the last one waits. The card shows "Saving — waiting". When the wait ends, the tray says "Already saved." with the reason. This is not a failure.

The **Configuration** tab also has a **Save now** button beside **Save unsaved home changes every**. It saves the home of the terminal user at once.

#### Merge layers

The button is on when the home has two or more layers, or one layer and unsaved changes. Otherwise it is off, with the tooltip "Nothing to merge: one layer and no unsaved changes".

1. Press **Merge layers**. If workspaces are open on that home, a card lists them with their agent icons and folders. Without open workspaces, a plain dialog appears: **Consolidate home layers?** "Save your unsaved changes and merge all saved layers into one layer. This saves memory."
2. Read the card. It says that your sessions close briefly and reopen where you left off.
3. Leave the box **Send Continue to each workspace after it reopens** ticked, or untick it. Unticked, the workspaces reopen with their conversation resumed but get no message. They then use no tokens (the paid units of an AI model) until you tell them to go on. This choice is for this merge only. It changes no setting. Untick the box when you plan to restart the server straight after the merge.
4. Press **Consolidate**. Expect: "Queued — watch the activity tray for progress."

> [!WARNING]
> A merge closes every open workspace of that home. A workspace that was working when it closed receives one Continue message after it reopens, unless you unticked the box. The plugin keeps each conversation and reopens it with Resume. Work that an agent was doing at that moment stops and restarts from the conversation. Save your own unsaved work in the agents first.

During a merge:

- A blue banner shows on the **Storage** tab and on the terminal page: "Storage tidy-up in progress".
- Each workspace of the home shows "Consolidating this home's storage… Session will resume automatically". Opening or reconnecting a workspace does not restart it until the merge ends. This lets the merge finish.
- Repair, merge, move, backup and restore are paused. If you press one, a message says that a consolidation is running.
- When the merge ends, the workspaces reopen by themselves.

#### Repair

The button **Repair** shows only when the home is not mounted. The status word reads **OFFLINE**.

1. Press **Repair**. Expect: **Repair home storage?** "Unmount and remount the OverlayFS stack ... This may briefly interrupt active sessions." (OverlayFS is the Linux feature that joins the layers into one folder.)
2. Press **Repair** in the dialog. Expect: **Repaired**, or **Repair Failed** with the reason.

Repair changes no data. It mounts the same layers again.

#### Delete

> [!WARNING]
> **Delete** removes all layers and session data of that home for good. You lose the agent sign-ins, settings, memory, chat transcripts and secrets of that user. Nothing of the home is kept. You cannot undo it. Snapshots in a backup folder are not part of the home and stay where they are.

1. Press the red button **Delete home…**. Expect: **Delete home data for 'name'?**
2. Press **Delete permanently**. For the primary homes (`root` and `aicliagent`), the dialog also asks you to type `DELETE` in a box. The plugin does not accept other text.
3. Expect: **Deleted**.

The plugin refuses to delete a home that a workspace is using. Close the workspaces first. It also refuses while a save, backup, restore, merge or convert for that home is queued or running. Wait for the job to end in the activity tray, then try again.

### Remove the old layers

After **Convert to plain folders**, the plugin keeps the old layers of the home for 14 days, so that a rollback is possible. While they exist, the home card shows the strip "Old layers kept for rollback: <size>, removed automatically on <date>". You do not have to do anything: the plugin removes the layers on that date. To get the space back sooner:

1. Press **Remove old layers** on the card. Expect: a dialog **Remove old layers?** with the size that you get back.
2. Press **Remove**. Expect: "Removed" and the strip disappears. Press **Cancel** to keep the layers.

This is the same removal as the **Remove** button of the line **Left over** on the **Boot disk space** card. The plugin checks again that nobody needs the layers. If a conversion of this home is still open, the strip does not show and the layers stay. The button is off while a job runs on the home. After you remove the layers, you can no longer roll the conversion back.

### Job states on the card

While a job runs, a small badge appears under the status word. The bar shows a moving stripe. The text has a verb and a state:

| Badge text | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Saving…**, **Merging layers…**, **Mounting…**, **Unmounting…**, **Repairing…**, **Deleting…**, **Backing up…**, **Restoring…** | The job runs now. The figures refresh when it ends. |
| The verb with "— queued" | The job waits behind another storage job. |
| The verb with "— waiting" (hourglass) | The job is put off. Hover the badge to read the reason. |

Two reasons appear for a put-off job. "This home was saved less than 30 minutes ago and is still in use" means the plugin saved a short time ago. "This home is in use" means a workspace holds the home. In both cases the plugin retries when the home is idle.

While a save or merge runs, the badge also shows an estimate such as "~1.15 GB to save" or "~1.15 GB to merge". It is the size of the unsaved data. Use it to judge progress, because the stripe moves slowly.

The card updates by itself from live messages. The page also reads the state again at intervals. A missed message corrects itself within about a minute.

### The Activity tray pill

Every save, merge, repair and delete shows a pill in the Activity tray at the bottom of the page. The pill has the same states as the card. A finished pill says "Done", or it explains why the memory did not drop. A put-off job says "Already saved." or "Could not finish." with a plain reason. A job that stopped with an error says "The storage job stopped with an error. Check the Debug Console log."

The tray text for a put-off save or merge reads: "Your data is already saved to disk. Freeing the RAM used by the previous copy is waiting for every open session on this home to close — it happens automatically the moment they do."

## Automatic saves

You do not need to press **Persist** often. The plugin saves by itself when one of these happens:

- **On a schedule.** The schedule is the **Save unsaved home changes every** field, described below.
- **When the last workspace of a home closes.** The save runs when the home is idle.
- **When much unsaved data builds up in RAM.** With the default settings, about 1 GB starts an immediate save of every home that has changes. At about 2 GB, Unraid shows a warning, "AICliAgents: High storage pressure". At a critical level (about 4 GB), Unraid shows "AICliAgents: Critical storage pressure" and the plugin does not start new workspaces until the data is saved. Workspaces that are open keep working. These limits are lower on a small RAM area, and they apply to a RAM writable layer only.
- **When you install or upgrade an agent.** The plugin saves the agent's files at once.
- **When the server stops.** See the section on array stop and shutdown.

A save that happens at an event restarts the timer. The plugin does not save twice in a row.

### The field "Save unsaved home changes every"

> [!NOTE]
> The field **Save unsaved home changes every** does not make a backup. It sets how often the plugin saves the writable layer into a layer. A backup is a separate, plain copy. See [Home backup and restore](backup-restore.md).

The field is in the **Configuration** tab. Its choices are every 15 minutes, every 30 minutes, every hour, every 2 hours, every 4 hours, every 8 hours, every 12 hours and once a day. The default is every 2 hours. The plugin saves only when the home has unsaved changes. The plugin keeps your choice as soon as you change it and uses it from its next check.

### The field "Merge layers after"

This number (from 4 to 40, default 30) is how many layers a home may build up. The plugin starts a merge at two layers below the ceiling (28 with the default), or sooner when disk space is low. A higher number gives fewer merges but a slower first load. Agents always use one layer.

### The notice to close workspaces

Sometimes the plugin needs a merge, but workspaces hold the home. This happens when the disk is nearly full or the RAM area is nearly full. The Activity tray then shows a notice, "Storage tidy-up needs your workspaces closed". It names the reason ("Disk space is low." or "Workspace memory is nearly full.") and lists the open workspaces.

- **Close all and tidy up** closes every workspace, saves their places, merges, and opens them again. A confirmation repeats this before anything closes.
- **Later** hides the notice for this wait. A later wait asks again. If the wait still goes on after 24 hours, the notice comes back.

A banner on the terminal page reads "Storage reclaim needed" until the tidy-up is done. When the last workspace closes, it reads "Storage tidy-up starting". You can minimise the banner. If you close the workspaces yourself, the tidy-up starts by itself.

For a home that can change to plain folders, the notice offers the conversion instead. Its title is "Convert this home to plain folders", and its button is **Convert to plain folders**. **Later** works the same way. The banner then reads "Home can change to plain folders" and has its own button **Convert to plain folders**. The button opens the same dialog as the notice, so you can convert even when you hid the notice. The notice stays when no workspace is open, because no automatic tidy-up runs for such a home. See "Convert a home to plain folders" above. When the plugin refuses the job, the row names the reason and the button works again. When the plugin does not answer, the row says "Could not reach the server."

### The field "Work folder for storage jobs"

This field is in the **Configuration** tab. It names a folder on a pool or an array disk. Storage jobs use it for temporary copies when the boot disk has no room: a merge uses it for database copies, and a conversion to plain folders uses it for the copy of the home and the old layers. Leave it empty and the plugin chooses a folder by itself, in this order: the Docker appdata folder, the VM domains folder, a protected pool with the most free space, any other disk with room. The plugin never uses RAM, `/tmp` or the boot disk. A value that points there is not saved.

### Caches of a plain-folder home

A tool such as npm or pip keeps downloaded files in cache folders. In a home with plain folders, these folders do not use the boot disk. They live in RAM, or in a folder on a pool. A cache is only a copy that a tool downloads again, so you lose nothing when it is empty.

The folders are `.npm`, `.cache`, `.bun/install/cache`, `.claude/cache`, `.claude/shell-snapshots`, `.claude/telemetry` and `tmp` in the home. The folder `.claude/plugins` is not a cache: it holds your installed Claude Code plugins, and it stays on the boot disk.

**Do not keep files you need in the folder `tmp` of your home.** The plugin treats `tmp` as a cache in every kind of home, also in a home with layers. A save leaves the files in `tmp` out of the saved layer, and the plugin can remove them when the home is idle. Put files that you want to keep in any other folder.

Three fields in the **Configuration** tab control this:

- **Caches of plain-folder homes**: **RAM** (the default) or **A folder on a pool**.
- **Cache folder on a pool**: the folder for the pool option, for example `/mnt/cache/aicli-caches`. Each home gets its own folder inside it. A user share (`/mnt/user`) is not accepted.
- **Memory for caches, per home**: the most RAM the caches of one home can use, from 256 to 8192 MB. The default is 1024 MB. The RAM is used only while the caches hold data. When a cache is full, the tool gets a "no space" error until you clear the caches.

When the pool is not mounted, for example while the array is stopped, the caches use RAM. When you stop the array, the plugin moves the caches from the pool to RAM first. If a program still has a file open in a cache at that moment, Unraid waits for it to close, as for any other open file on the pool; the plugin log names the program. When the array starts again, the caches go back to the pool the next time the home starts.

The first time a home starts after this feature is on, the plugin removes the old cache content from the boot disk once. It does this only while no workspace of that home runs. The Activity tray shows how much space it freed.

**Clear caches** (on the line **Home** *name*: **caches** of the **Boot disk space** card; see "Boot disk space") empties the cache folders of a home. The dialog shows the size it frees, from the last measure, with the time of that measure. The button works only while no workspace of that home runs. A home with layers is not changed: the merge of layers already drops its caches.

## Boot disk space

The plugin keeps its homes and agents on the boot disk, because they must work while the array is stopped. A boot disk is small. The card **Boot disk space** on the **Storage** tab shows where the space goes and what frees it. Its status line reads, for example, "5.7 GB used of 15 GB · 8.6 GB free". The **(i)** in its header says how to read the card. A small **(i)** beside the name of a line holds the note of that line; for a cache line it also has a link **Go to setting**. The buttons of the card have the same look and the same 44 px height on a phone as the other buttons of the page.

The card shows a bar with the size of the boot disk, how much is used and how much is free. Below the bar is one line for each part, the largest first. Each line has a bar, its size and, when there is something to do, a button. The sizes are the space really used on the disk, so compression is counted.

The plugin measures the sizes in the background, never while you wait. A measure can take a few minutes on a slow disk. It runs with the lowest priority and has a time limit of 5 minutes. If the limit ends the measure early, the card says that some sizes may be missing. The card shows the time of the last measure ("Measured at 14:05"). The plugin measures again when the last measure is more than 10 minutes old, and after an action on the card. Press **Measure now** to measure when you want. While a measure runs, the card says "measuring now" and updates by itself.

The dialogs of the buttons (**Remove old versions**, **Clear caches**, **Convert to plain folders**, **Move old sessions…**) read the numbers of the last measure. Each dialog shows when the numbers were measured. When they are more than 10 minutes old, or missing, the dialog also shows **Measure now**. The dialog never measures by itself.

A button is grey when the action cannot run now. Hold the mouse over it to read the reason, for example "No old version to remove." or "Agents on a USB boot stick keep compressed layers."

### The lines

| Line | What it counts | Button |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Home** *name*: **conversation history** | The sessions that the agents keep in the home. | **Move old sessions…**. After a move, **Bring back…** also shows. See "Move old conversation sessions". |
| **Home** *name*: **caches** | The cache content that is still on the boot disk. A note says where the cache lives now (RAM or a pool). | **Clear caches**. A link **Cache setting** opens the field **Caches of plain-folder homes**. See "Caches of a plain-folder home". |
| **Home** *name*: **other** | The rest of the home: your own files and agent settings. | None. |
| **Home** *name*: **quarantine** | Damaged agent databases that the plugin set aside and replaced. Shown only when the folder holds something. | **Archive…** and **Remove**. See "Archive or remove old data of a home". |
| **Home** *name*: **data of deleted OpenCode workspaces** | OpenCode keeps one database for each workspace. This line counts the data of workspaces that are not in your workspace list or your favourites any more. Included in the **conversation history** line. | **Archive…** and **Remove**. |
| **Home** *name*: **large Codex session logs** | Codex session logs of 1 MB or more that did not change for 14 days. Included in the **conversation history** line. | **Archive…** and **Remove**. |
| **Home** *name*: **large session logs of other agents** | Sessions of Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, Kimi Code and Antigravity CLI that are 1 MB or more in total and did not change for 14 days. Included in the **conversation history** line. | **Archive…** and **Remove**. |
| **Home** *name*: **saved layers** | A home that uses layers: the saved layers and the writable layer. | **Close all and tidy up**. It merges the layers. See "Merge layers". |
| **Agents: current versions** | The agents in use. A note names each agent and whether it uses layers or plain folders. | **Convert to plain folders**, when the plugin offers it. See "Convert agents to plain folders". |
| **Agents: old versions** | The previous versions that are kept for a roll back, plain folders and layers. | **Remove old versions**. See "Remove old versions now". |
| **Left over** | Old layers that a conversion moved aside (they stay for 14 days), an unfinished conversion copy, the layers of a home that no workspace uses, old layer images that a newer merged layer replaced (one item for each home or agent), and the test homes that the smoke tests left. A home of the configured user, or of an Unraid user, is never listed here, even when its name looks like a test name. Layers that an open conversion still needs are marked **needed to finish or roll back a conversion** and cannot be removed. | **Remove**. When old layer images are listed, also **Archive layer images…**. See "Archive old layer images". |
| **Plugin files** | The rest of the plugin folder: program files, saved copies of earlier versions, settings and state. | None. |

A home in plain folders has the first three **Home** lines. A home with layers has the line **saved layers**.

### Remove left-over items

1. Press **Remove** on the line **Left over**. Expect: a dialog **Remove left-over items?** It names each item with its size, and the total space it frees.
2. Press **Remove** to continue, or **Cancel** to stop. Expect: after **Remove**, a dialog says how much space you got back, and the card measures again.

The plugin checks each item again just before it removes it. It removes only items that the last measure listed under **Left over**. It keeps an item that a mount or a program uses, and says so. It also keeps old layers that an open conversion needs to finish or roll back.

An **Unfinished conversion copy** is a partial copy left by a failed storage migration when the plugin could not remove it. The plugin checks its marker and path again before it removes the copy.

An item **Old layer images that a newer merged layer replaced** is a layer file of a home or an agent that the layer list no longer names, because a merge replaced it. Nothing reads such a file. The plugin lists a file only when all of these are true: the layer list names a merged layer that is newer than the file; no mount and no program uses the file; no merge or conversion of that home or agent is running; and the file is more than one hour old. A newer layer that the layer list does not name yet is never listed, because a save may be on its way. **Remove** deletes only the listed files of that item.

### Archive or remove old data of a home

Four lines of the card can move old data off the boot disk. Each line has a small **i** mark (hold the mouse over it for a short note) and two buttons.

- **quarantine**: databases that an agent set aside because they were damaged.
- **data of deleted OpenCode workspaces**: OpenCode data of workspaces that you deleted. Data of a workspace that is in your list, or is a favourite, is never listed.
- **large Codex session logs**: Codex logs of 1 MB or more, not changed for 14 days. Codex cannot resume a session that you archive or remove. These logs are also counted in the line **conversation history**. For many agents at once, use **Move old sessions…**, which can bring sessions back.
- **large session logs of other agents**: the same rule for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, Kimi Code and Antigravity CLI. The files of one session count together, and the session is as new as its newest file. An agent cannot resume a session that you archive or remove, unless you restore it. The agents that keep their history in one database (OpenCode, Kilo Code, Goose) have no such line, because a database cannot be split into sessions.

To archive:

1. Make a folder inside a pool first, for example `/mnt/datapool/backups`. The plugin does not make new folders at the top of a pool, because Unraid shows each one as a share.
2. Press **Archive…** on the line. Expect: a dialog with the size and the number of items.
3. Pick the pool and type the name of the folder. Expect: the line **Files go to** shows the full place, `…/aicliagents-archive/<server name>/<date>/`.
4. Press **Archive**. Expect: a message "Archive started". The Activity tray shows the progress.

The plugin copies each file, checks the copy with a SHA-256 value, writes a list of the files (a manifest file) in the archive, and only then removes the file from the boot disk. If a copy does not match, the original stays. The plugin never writes over a different file in the archive. The folder must be on a mounted pool. A folder on the boot disk, in RAM or under `/mnt/user` is refused, and so is the pool itself.

To remove, press **Remove** on the line. Expect: a dialog that names the items and the space it frees. Press **Remove** to continue. Nothing is copied first, so the data is gone for good. Use **Archive…** when you may want it later.

In both cases the plugin leaves an item alone when a program has one of its files open, or when OpenCode data changed in the last day. The line then says how many items it left. If the workspace list is empty or unreadable, the plugin offers no OpenCode data at all, because it cannot tell which data is in use. The buttons are grey during a storage migration.

### Archive old layer images

The line **Left over** can list **Old layer images that a newer merged layer replaced**. Next to **Remove** it then has **Archive layer images…**. Use it when you want to keep a copy of these files before they go.

1. Make a folder inside a pool first, as for any archive.
2. Press **Archive layer images…** on the line **Left over**. Expect: a dialog with the size and the number of homes and agents. It says that the plugin does not put an archived image back.
3. Pick the pool and the folder. Press **Archive**. Expect: a message "Archive started" and a progress entry **Archive old layer images** in the Activity tray.

The plugin copies each file, checks the copy, writes the list of files, and only then removes the file from the boot disk. Just before each file goes, the plugin checks again that no mount and no program uses it, and that the layer list still does not name it. A file that is in use stays on the boot disk, and its copy stays in the archive. The plugin does not restore this kind of archive: an old layer image is not in the layer list, so the plugin could not use it. The copy is for safekeeping.

### Large writes stop before the boot disk is too full

The plugin does not start a large write to the boot disk when it would make the disk more than 85 % full. This covers packing an agent, installing an agent, a change of **Home storage** or **Agent storage**, **Restore from an archive…** and **Bring back…**. Small writes, such as settings, are not stopped. Saving a home as a new layer and merging layers are never held back by this level: they stop only when the disk is really full.

When a write is stopped, the plugin writes nothing. The Activity tray shows an entry, for example "Not started: the restore from an archive needs 600 MB on the boot disk. The boot disk is 82 % full, and this would make it 88 % full. The plugin keeps it below 85 %. Free at least 300 MB first." Free some space with the buttons of this card, then try again. Act on the warning at 80 %, before the disk is really full.

An agent can ask for the same actions with the tools `aicli_archive_boot_data` and `aicli_remove_boot_data`. They only propose: nothing moves until you approve the item in the Activity tray. `aicli_get_boot_space` lists the lines.

### Restore from an archive

Press **Restore from an archive…** at the bottom of the card to put archived files back into a home. The plugin never overwrites a file in the home unless you choose so.

1. Press **Restore from an archive…**. Expect: a dialog with a pool and a folder. The pool and folder of your last move are filled in.
2. Pick the pool and the folder that you used when you archived. Press **Find archives**. Expect: a list of archives, newest first, each with its date, the server name, the kind of data and the home.
3. Pick one archive. Press **Check this archive**. Expect: after a short wait, a list that says how many files are **new** (not in the home, will be copied), **the same** (already in the home with the same content, nothing to do) and **different** (in the home with other content). The list shows which file in the home is newer. A file that cannot be restored is named with the reason.
4. If some files are different, choose what happens to them. **Keep the files in the home** is the default. **Replace them with the archived files** copies the archived file over the file in the home.
5. Press **Restore**. Expect: a message "Restore started". The Activity tray shows the progress and the result. Nothing is copied before this step.

The check only reads. The restore copies each file, checks the copy with its SHA-256 value from the manifest, and then puts it in place. The archive stays as it is. The plugin does not replace a file that a program has open. It refuses a file whose path lies outside the home or outside the folder the file came from, and a file whose archived copy is missing or damaged. The buttons are grey during a storage migration.

### The warning when the boot disk is nearly full

When the boot disk is 80% full, the card **Boot disk space** shows a warning in its header and under the bar, and the Activity tray gets one notice. This early warning sends no Unraid notification. At 85% the plugin also sends an Unraid notification, once in 6 hours, so one rise from 80% to 86% gives you one notification. The warning ends when the disk falls below 77%. The text names the biggest users, and the advice fits the biggest part:

- Layers are the biggest: "Close all and tidy up merges the layers and frees space."
- A home in plain folders is the biggest: "Conversation history and caches use most of it. Move old sessions or clear caches."
- Old agent versions are the biggest: "Remove old agent versions frees space."
- The agents are the biggest: "The agents use most of it. Remove old agent versions to free space."

Each warning ends with "Open Storage, Boot disk space." The notification is a link: a click opens the **Storage** tab at the card.

## Temporary files of agents in RAM

Agents write temporary files, for example git clones, to a temporary folder. On Unraid that folder is RAM. A large temporary folder uses the memory of the server and can make typing slow.

When the temporary files of agents in RAM pass the limit, the card **Boot disk space** shows an orange warning. The limit is the setting **Warn when temporary files in memory pass** (default 1024 MB). The warning names the size and how much of it belongs to sessions that no longer run.

1. Press **Clean up temporary files of closed sessions**. Expect: a dialog names the size it frees and the age of the numbers.
2. Press **Clean up** to continue, or **Cancel** to stop. Expect: a message says that the clean-up is queued. The Activity tray shows the steps ("Looking for closed sessions", "Removing temporary files of closed sessions") and the result.

The clean-up removes only the temporary files of sessions that ended at least a day ago: nothing in them changed for 24 hours. A session that runs stays. The whole temporary folder of a project stays while a program works in that project, or a workspace of the plugin uses it, even when one session in it is idle. Your projects and your home are not touched.

To keep new sessions from filling RAM, set **Agent temporary files** on the **Configuration** tab to **A folder on a pool**. A new session then keeps its temporary files there.

## Old agent versions

Each agent keeps its last version so you can roll back. The old versions use space on the boot disk. The plugin removes the oldest ones by itself. You can also remove them at once.

### The setting "Keep the previous agent version"

This setting is in the **Configuration** tab, card **Storage**. The default is **Yes**: each agent keeps its last version, so you can roll back. Choose **No** to keep only the version in use. The plugin then removes the previous version at its next clean-up, and you save space on the boot disk. A version that a running workspace uses always stays.

### Remove old versions now

Press **Remove old versions** in the storage line of an installed agent card in the **Agent Store** tab. The card **Boot disk space** shows the same action for all agents, on the line **Agents: old versions**. See "Boot disk space".

1. Press **Remove old versions**. Expect: a dialog lists the old versions of the agent, the space the removal frees, and the versions that stay because a workspace uses them. The dialog names the workspace. It shows when the list was measured; press **Measure now** when the list is old.
2. Press **Remove** to continue, or **Cancel** to stop. Expect: after **Remove**, the dialog says "Removal queued". The Activity tray shows the steps ("Checking the old versions", "Removing old versions") and ends with how much space you got back. The card measures again by itself.

The action removes old version folders, old storage layers and the kept rollback copies. When the setting above is **Yes**, the newest kept rollback copy stays. After the removal, you cannot roll back to a removed version. A version that a workspace uses is never removed. If a clean-up of that agent already runs, the plugin leaves that item and says so; press the link again later.

## Move old conversation sessions

Each agent keeps your conversations in your home on the boot disk. Old conversations can use a lot of space: on one test server, Codex used 2.1 GB and Claude Code 0.8 GB. You can move the old ones to a folder on a pool, and bring them back later.

The line **Home** *name*: **conversation history** of the card **Boot disk space** (see "Boot disk space") has the button **Move old sessions…**. The button opens a dialog.

1. Choose the agent, or **All agents that keep one file for each session**. An agent that keeps its history in a database (OpenCode, Kilo Code and Goose) is grey. The dialog shows its size and says that it cannot move.
2. Enter the age in days. The default is 90. The dialog shows how many sessions are older, and how much space they use. It has these counts for 30, 90 and 180 days, from the last measure. For another age it says so; the move still works for any age.
3. Choose a pool and a folder name. The plugin remembers the folder in the setting **Folder for moved sessions**.
4. Read the warning: "Moved sessions cannot be resumed, and are not reachable while the array is stopped."
5. Select **Move sessions**. The Activity tray shows the progress, for example "Moving sessions: 12 of 140 files (3.0 GB)".

The plugin copies each file, checks the copy, and only then removes the original. It never moves a file that a program has open or that changed in the last 24 hours. It never deletes a session. If the array is stopped, the dialog says "The array is stopped" and nothing moves. If a move stops at one agent, the Activity tray names the agents that were not reached. Their sessions stay in the home.

The folder you chose then holds `<user>/<agent>/…` with the moved files and a list, `MOVED.json`, with the size and the check value of each file.

To get sessions back, select **Bring back…** on the same line. It shows after you moved sessions. The plugin copies the files into your home again, checks them, and removes them from the folder. It never replaces a file that is already in your home. Some agents (for example Codex and GitHub Copilot) keep an index of their sessions. The index stays, so a moved session can still be listed there but it does not open until you bring it back.

## What happens when the array stops or the server shuts down

### Stop the array

If your home storage or agent storage is on the array or on a pool, the plugin adds a step when you press **Stop** on Unraid's Main page. A dialog, **AI CLI Agents Affected**, lists:

- the storage paths on the array or pool;
- every open session whose workspace folder is under `/mnt/` (except `/mnt/disks` and `/mnt/remotes`).

It warns that a temporary home will be used while the array is stopped, and that changes made in Emergency Mode are discarded when the array starts again. It also warns that the listed sessions will be ended to prevent unmount locks.

Press **Proceed & Stop Array** to go on, or **Cancel**. If your storage is on the USB flash drive and no workspace folder is under `/mnt/`, the plugin shows nothing and the array stops as usual.

### Reboot or power off

When Unraid stops, the plugin does these steps, in this order:

1. It stops the automatic merging.
2. It asks each agent to end, and waits up to five seconds. This lets the agent finish its database writes.
3. It saves the unsaved changes of each home into a layer. It does not save agent storage, because the agent files are saved at install time.
4. It unmounts the layers, so that Unraid can stop the disks.

A shutdown never merges layers. It only adds one layer for each home.

The time limit for these steps comes from Unraid. It is the **Shutdown time-out** in Settings, Disk Settings, minus 15 seconds, and at least 30 seconds. With Unraid's default of 90 seconds, the plugin has about 75 seconds. A very large home may not finish saving in that time. Then a little unsaved data in RAM can be lost. A shorter **Save unsaved home changes every** reduces that risk. A power cut gives no time at all: with the RAM writable layer, you lose changes since the last save. The disk writable layer keeps them.

## Emergency Mode

Emergency Mode lets you keep working when storage is missing, for example when the array is stopped and your home lives on it. You work in a temporary home. The plugin does not save it.

When storage is missing, the terminal page shows a yellow panel **Storage Unavailable**. The drawer button changes from **New Workspace** to **Emergency Session**.

- If agent storage is still there, the panel shows **Start Emergency Session**. It opens a workspace with a temporary home. Above the button the panel says: "Work done in an emergency session is temporary. It is lost when storage returns."
- If agent storage is missing too, the panel shows a list of agents and the button **Install to RAM**. The plugin installs the chosen agent into RAM and starts a session at once. OpenCode is the suggested choice, because it needs no sign-in and includes free models. The installed agent is lost when the array starts again.

A yellow banner shows in the session: "Emergency Mode — Temporary home. Work done here is not saved and is lost when storage returns. When storage returns this session closes and your saved state is restored."

If you press **Persist** while the session runs on the temporary home, the plugin shows the warning **Not saved**. It does not save the temporary home.

When the storage returns, the page reloads by itself. Copy anything you need out of the temporary session before that.

## When the plugin halts a home: "Storage Attention Needed"

At start-up the plugin checks that the layers on disk match its record of them. If they do not, it will not mount an empty home on top of your data. A full-page card appears with the title **AI CLI Agents: Storage Attention Needed**. It says that your data has not been changed and that the plugin does not overwrite it without your consent.

Each card names the item (for example Home storage "root"), says what is wrong, and carries a **HALTED** badge.

| Message | What it means | Buttons you may see |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Saved layers were found in another folder that the plugin does not manage | Your layers exist, but not where the plugin looks. | **Restore from** the folder |
| The plugin saved these layers in one folder, but the storage setting now points to another folder, so it cannot find them | Someone changed the storage path without a move. | **Restore from** the folder. **Open Settings** may show. |
| Some saved layers are missing from the storage folder | The record lists layers that are not on disk. | **Start fresh and abandon data** (homes) |
| All saved layers are missing. The drive may be disconnected | The drive may be unplugged, or the array is stopped. | **Start fresh and abandon data** (homes) |
| A saved layer failed its integrity check (the checksum does not match) | A layer file is damaged. | Often only the two buttons that every card has. **Override and start fresh** may show. |
| The saved layers were written on a different server (the USB flash drive may have moved) | The flash drive belongs to another machine in the plugin's record. | **Confirm: this is the correct machine** |

Every card also has **Retry integrity check** and **Dismiss for 24h**.

- **Retry integrity check** runs the check again. Use it after you plug a drive back in or start the array. If the problem is gone, the card disappears.
- **Dismiss for 24h** hides the card on this device for 24 hours. The problem stays. Reload the page after 24 hours, or press retry, to see it again.
- **Restore from** moves the layer files from the folder it names into the active storage path and records them. Use it when the layers are intact. Expect: "Restored", and the plugin can mount the home.
- **Confirm: this is the correct machine** tells the plugin that the flash drive is in the right server. Use it only when you know this is true.
- **Start fresh and abandon data** and **Override and start fresh** let the plugin mount an empty home.

> [!WARNING]
> **Start fresh and abandon data** deletes all existing layers of that home for good. You lose the sign-ins, memory and transcripts it holds. The plugin asks you to type `WIPE` before it goes on. **Override and start fresh** asks for a plain confirmation and allows an empty mount. Try **Retry integrity check**, **Restore from** and a backup first.

For agent storage, the plugin heals itself. If every layer of an agent is missing, a card shows **HEALING** and "Reinstalling agent…". The plugin installs the agent again. No data is lost, because agent storage holds only program files.

The boot check also removes the leftover record of a throwaway test home when its temporary folder is gone. This applies only to homes under the plugin's temporary appdata folder. A home on a pool, the array or the flash drive is never removed this way, even when its drive is missing.

The **Storage** tab shows a related banner when the boot check finds something that does not need a full-page halt: "Boot integrity — N entities need attention". For a home it shows **Restore from sibling**. For an agent it shows **Show on Agent Store →**, which opens the agent's card.

## Health warnings about storage

The Health dot at the top of the Settings page turns amber when a storage check finds a problem. Press the (i) next to it to read the text. Click the dot to open the **Debug Console** tab. Two checks cover the layers.

### Deleted layers still pin space

After a merge, the plugin deletes the old layer files. The disk space does not come back while something still uses the old copy. The check warns at 512 MB or more: "Deleted layers still pin N MB of the boot drive (N loop devices)." (A loop device is the Linux way to mount a file as a disk.)

- If the text names workspaces, they still use an old copy of the home. Restart them to free the space.
- If it names none, no workspace holds the space. The space frees at the next restart of the server.

The check only reads. It never ends a process, detaches a device or restarts a workspace.

### A large writable layer on a filling boot drive

With the **Disk** writable layer, a home on the boot drive keeps its changes there. The layer grows while agents work, and only a merge empties it. The check warns when the boot drive is 70 percent full or more and a home's writable layer on it holds 512 MB or more.

The text names the homes and gives the three ways out:

1. Merge the home. Press **Consolidate** on its card. This closes open workspaces.
2. Move the writable layer to RAM. See the setting above.
3. Move the home off the boot drive. See the section on moving storage.

The plugin never starts a merge by itself for this warning, because a merge closes your workspaces.

### RAM caches use much of the RAM

A third check covers the RAM caches of plain-folder homes. It warns when the **Memory for caches, per home** of all such homes together is more than 25 percent of the RAM of the server. The text says how many homes it counts. Lower **Memory for caches, per home**, or choose **A folder on a pool** for **Caches of plain-folder homes**. The check only reads.

## What happens behind the scenes

The plugin saves the writable layer with a method that keeps databases safe. Many agents keep a database that is spread over several files. A plain copy at the wrong moment would give a broken database. The plugin copies each such database with SQLite's own safe-copy feature, so the saved copy is complete. The plugin keeps a list of every layer and checks each layer when it mounts. That list is why the start-up check can tell you what is missing. For the full design, see C4 Component: Storage Management.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| The card shows **OFFLINE** | The home is not mounted. | Press **Repair**. If it fails, check that the drive is present and press **Retry integrity check**. |
| "Saving — waiting" for a long time | The home is in use, or it was saved less than 30 minutes ago. | Wait. The data is already on disk. Close the workspaces of that home to free the memory. |
| The status word shows a large "MB volatile" and does not drop after a save | Open workspaces hold the old copy of the home in memory. | Close the workspaces, or press **Consolidate** at a quiet time. |
| The Consolidate icon is grey | The home has one layer and no unsaved changes. | Nothing to do. |
| A message "Storage tidy-up in progress" blocks a button | A merge is running. | Wait a few minutes. The workspaces reopen by themselves. |
| An amber note "Recent consolidate failure" shows on the **Storage** tab | A merge failed. The plugin retries by itself. After two failures in a row it halts automatic merges for that home. | Read the Debug Console log. Ask for help on the forum if the note stays. |
| An Unraid notice "AICliAgents: not enough boot disk space to save the home", or the tray entry **Not enough boot disk space to save the home** | The boot disk has too little free space for the new layer, so the plugin wrote nothing. Your changes are still only in RAM and are lost if the server restarts. The plugin first tests the layer at the compression of your last saved layer, so it refuses only when even that size does not fit. | Free some space on the boot disk (the card **Boot disk space** shows what uses it), then press **Persist** again. The notice and the tray entry end by themselves after the next good save. |
| **Not moved** after you change the writable layer | A home was in use or had no room. The setting went back. | Read the reason, free space or close the workspace, and try again. |
| "Path must include a sub-directory under the Unassigned Device mount" | You chose the top folder of an Unassigned Devices drive. | Create a folder on the drive, for example `aicliagents`, and choose that folder. |
| **Storage Unavailable** on the terminal page | The array is stopped, or the drive is gone. | Start the array or plug in the drive, or use **Emergency Session**. |
| A full-page **Storage Attention Needed** card | The start-up check found a mismatch. | See the table in the halt section. Do not choose **Start fresh** before you try **Restore from** and a backup. |
| An Unraid notice "AICliAgents: a saved layer of your home was damaged" | The newest saved layer of the home is empty or is not a valid file. The plugin moved it to the folder `.bad` inside the storage folder and started the home without it. Only the changes saved in that layer are missing. The file is not deleted. | Check your recent work. Keep the file in `.bad` until you are sure that you do not need it. |
| A workspace does not start and the Debug Console says "Layer … cannot be mounted" | One saved layer of the home cannot be read. The message names the layer and the reason. The plugin does not skip a layer in the middle of the stack, because the newer layers depend on it. The file is not changed. | Ask for help on the forum and give the layer name. Do not delete the file. |
| A Health warning about pinned space | Old layers hold disk space. | Restart the workspaces that the text names, or restart the server. |
| A card **Legacy Migration Artifacts** shows on the **Storage** tab | Old files from a past storage conversion are still on disk. | Check that your agents and workspaces work. Then press **Purge All Artifacts**. This deletes the files for good. |
| A dialog or a button on the **Storage** tab shows "Could not reach the server" | The browser could not reach the plugin, or the server answered with an error. The message says which. | Check that the server is up and the Unraid login is still open. Reload the page and try again. A button that was waiting, such as **Measure now**, works again. |
| A second click on **Back up now**, **Restore**, **Consolidate**, **Convert** or **Remove old versions** says the job "is already waiting or running" | The same job for the same home or agent is already in the queue. | Watch the Activity tray. Press the button again after the job ends. |
